composer.optimizingHint: Please wait, optimizing file to save tokens...
composer.placeholder: Ask Cerne Code to read, edit or run something in your project...
composer.executionModeTooltip: YOLO: edits directly, no sandbox. Automatic: sandbox + you accept/reject. Manual: approve every action.
composer.reasoningTooltip: Model reasoning. 💤 Off = no thinking (faster, default for local models). Auto = the model decides.
composer.fableTooltip: Fable method (for small/medium models): turns on a classify → act → verify loop so the model doesn't abandon tasks. Off by default; on large models it just bloats the prompt.

toolLabels.grep: Searched for a pattern in files
toolLabels.computer_use_focus_window: Brought a window to the foreground

skillEditor.whatIsASkill: What a skill is: a SKILL.md file with instructions the agent loads on demand (via load_skill) when it notices they're relevant to the current request — a way to teach the agent a specific step-by-step process or convention without having to rewrite it every conversation.
skillEditor.whenToCreateOne: When it's worth creating one: when you catch yourself explaining the same thing to the agent across different conversations (a team process, a specific output format, the right steps to review a PR, etc.). The description is what the agent reads to decide whether the skill is relevant — make it clearly state WHEN to use it.
skillEditor.fillNameAndDescription: Fill in the name and "when to use it" before saving.

extraReadPaths.title: Extra read folders
extraReadPaths.hint: The agent can read (not edit) files from these folders, in addition to the project folder.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Changes the language of the entire interface — messages, labels, titles and skills.
settings.activeProviderHint: Choose where Cerne Code sources inference from for new sessions.
settings.apiKeyVaultHint: API key saved in the system's credential vault (never in plain text).
settings.llamaCppHint: Forks configured in providers.toml — each one points to the llama-server.exe and models.ini of a specific llama.cpp build on your machine. No fork comes pre-configured (Cerne Code ships without assuming where you installed yours).
settings.customProvidersHint: Any endpoint compatible with OpenAI's chat completions API — Claude (via https://api.anthropic.com/v1/), Grok/xAI (https://api.x.ai/v1), ChatGPT/OpenAI (https://api.openai.com/v1), Qwen/DashScope, Kimi/Moonshot, or any other. Shows up in the sessions' provider picker with the label you give it.
settings.visionEnabledConnection: Image support enabled on this connection
settings.idCannotChange: The id identifies the provider, it can't be changed by editing
settings.newApiKeyPlaceholder: new API key (leave blank to keep the current one)
settings.visionCheckboxLabel: Models on this connection accept images (manual confirmation — can't be confirmed automatically on a generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
settings.contextLengthPlaceholder: context size in tokens (optional — most custom endpoints don't report this)
settings.skillsHint: Folders with SKILL.md that the agent discovers on its own and loads on demand (load_skill). Project skills (<project>/.cerne/skills/) only show up here from inside the session — this list shows the global ones.
settings.noSkillsYet: No skills yet besides the README.
settings.mcpHintBefore: External tools via Model Context Protocol — each server runs as a subprocess (stdio) and its tools show up to the agent as
settings.mcpHintAfter3: object-by-name format that most MCP servers already document ready to paste in.
settings.nameCannotChange: The name identifies the server, it can't be changed by editing — remove and recreate it if you need to rename it
settings.envVarsPlaceholder: environment variables, one per line (e.g. GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...)
settings.webSearchHint: By default (Automatic) the web_search tool uses DuckDuckGo directly — no install, no API key. If you'd rather use a paid API's results (Brave, Tavily) or already run your own SearXNG instance, you can switch here.
settings.keyAlreadyConfigured: key already configured — leave blank to keep it
settings.connectedResultsFound: Connected! {count} result(s) found in a test search.

help.title: Help
help.hint: Clicking Use pastes the prompt into your chat — feel free to edit it before sending.

search-summarize.title: Research and summarize a topic
search-summarize.preview: Searches a topic on the web and summarizes the main points found.
search-summarize.full: Search the web about [TOPIC] and write a summary of the main points found. Cite the sources.

read-large-file.title: Read a large file in chunks
read-large-file.preview: Reads a large file in chunks using offset/limit, without blowing the context.
read-large-file.full: Read the file [PATH] in chunks: start with read_file(path="[PATH]", offset=0, limit=200) and keep advancing 200 lines at a time. Summarize the content of each section.

create-file.title: Create a new file
create-file.preview: Creates a new file with the specified content in the project.
create-file.full:
Create a file at [PATH] with the following content:

[DESCRIBE THE CONTENT]

edit-file.title: Edit a snippet in a file
edit-file.preview: Modifies a specific snippet in an existing file.
edit-file.full: In the file [PATH], find the snippet [OLD SNIPPET] and replace it with [NEW SNIPPET].

run-command.title: Run a terminal command
run-command.preview: Runs a shell command and shows the result.
run-command.full:
Run the command: [COMMAND]

Explain the result.

computer-use.title: Automate a task on screen
computer-use.preview: Automates clicks and typing on screen to carry out a repetitive task.
computer-use.full:
Use computer_use to: [DESCRIBE THE SCREEN TASK].

Take a screenshot first to see the current state, then carry out the necessary steps.

create-excel.title: Generate an Excel spreadsheet
create-excel.preview: Creates a .xlsx file with tabs, formatted headers and data.
create-excel.full:
Create an Excel spreadsheet at [PATH.xlsx] with the following columns: [COLUMNS].
Include the data: [DATA].
Format the headers in bold and turn on autofilter.

create-word.title: Generate a Word document
create-word.preview: Creates a .docx file with titles, paragraphs, tables and lists.
create-word.full:
Create a Word document at [PATH.docx] with:
- A title: [TITLE]
- Paragraphs with the content: [CONTENT]
- A table with columns [COLUMNS] and data [DATA]

create-pdf.title: Generate a PDF report
create-pdf.preview: Creates a PDF document with titles, paragraphs and tables.
create-pdf.full:
Create a PDF at [PATH.pdf] with the title "[TITLE]".
Include the sections: [SECTIONS].
Add a table with [COLUMNS] and [DATA].

refactor-code.title: Refactor code with AST
refactor-code.preview: Finds and replaces code patterns using syntactic (AST) analysis.
refactor-code.full:
Use ast_grep to find every occurrence of [PATTERN] in the project.
Then use ast_edit to replace it with [NEW PATTERN].

subagent-task.title: Delegate a parallel task
subagent-task.preview: Creates a sub-agent to solve an independent task in parallel.
subagent-task.full:
Use the task tool to create a sub-agent that: [DESCRIBE THE TASK].
The sub-agent should work independently and report the result.

plan-todo.title: Plan a complex task
plan-todo.preview: Creates a visual plan with steps for a complex task.
plan-todo.full:
Plan the following task using todo_list: [DESCRIBE THE COMPLEX TASK].
Break it into clear steps and carry out each one.

grep-search.title: Search for a term in the project
grep-search.preview: Searches for a term or regex across all project files.
grep-search.full:
Search for "[TERM]" in every file in the project using grep.
List the files and lines where it appears.

fetch-page.title: Extract content from a URL
fetch-page.preview: Fetches the content of a web page and extracts the relevant information.
fetch-page.full: Visit [URL] and extract the main information from the page. Summarize the content.
